text.p: The central bank injected a total of 41.9 trillion lira on Wednesday via overnight lending and an open market t-bill repurchase auction to relieve the cash squeeze seen over the past five weeks.

It lent banks 31.4 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent after buying 10.5 trillion lira of eight-day repos in the morning at an average annual rate of 73.63 percent, up from 73.50 percent at Tuesday's nine-day repo auction.
Overnight money also traded at 74.75 percent during the day before the central bank stepped in. The bank had lent a total of 16.8 trillion lira via overnight lending and repo auction on Tuesday.
The lira closed firmer at 95,260 to the dollar from Tuesday's 95,350 close as weaker dollar/mark parity was dominant in a demanding domestic market.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 95,000 lira at the opening, down from 95,050 at Tuesday's close. It further decreased the rate during the day to close it at 94,900 lira.
Yields on t-bills with 1997 maturity eased around one point across the board.
Bankers said the market expects the Treasury to open an auction on Friday with a maturity date longer than June 1997 which fueled demand for long-term t-bills.
On the other hand, short-term t-bill yields firmed by one point amid a cash squeeze.

The Treasury usually holds auctions on Tuesdays, but Turkish markets will be closed from noon on Monday until Wednesday next week due to an official holiday. Next Wednesday, the Treasury will repay 140 trillion of t-bill maturities.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4 fell to 120.64 percent from Tuesday's 121.85 percent. The second most active May 7 paper yielded 117.20 percent, down from yesterday's 118.86 percent average. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
